headline: Democrats win Congress, Canada’s budget lands, U.S. strikes on Iran continue
summary: Democrats flipped Congress in the Nov. 3 midterms, and Trump responded by replacing his chief of staff with Stephen Miller. Canada tabled its budget and lost jobs in October, while the U.S.–Iran conflict kept oil prices elevated.

top.headline: Democrats flip Congress; final House and Senate counts still firming up
top.what: Networks project Democrats will hold at least 259 House seats and at least 54 Senate seats; the Alaska and Mississippi Senate races are unresolved, with lawyers now involved in a razor-thin Mississippi count.
top.why: Changes how Washington works for the next two years, including on tariffs.

top.headline: Trump confirms new ‘minor’ US strikes on Iran, says talks are progressing
top.what: President Trump said the U.S. carried out another round of limited strikes on Iran’s Qeshm Island while claiming progress in talks to end the war.
top.why: Drives oil and gas prices that Ontario drivers and businesses feel.

top.headline: Carney government's second budget projects $62.3B deficit with $142B in new spending
top.what: Finance Minister Champagne tabled the budget Thursday: a $62.3-billion deficit for 2026-27 and about $142 billion in new spending over five years.
top.why: Sets federal spending, deficits and immigration levels.

top.headline: Canada-U.S. trade talks continue as Democrats vow to repeal tariffs
top.what: Tariffs on Canadian goods remain while talks continue, and the DNC chair says Democrats would move to end them if they win power.
top.why: Tariffs on Canadian goods affect Ontario manufacturing jobs.

top.headline: Trump names Stephen Miller White House chief of staff, replacing Susie Wiles
top.what: Days after heavy Republican midterm losses, Trump said Miller, a lead architect of his immigration crackdown, will take over as chief of staff on Monday, Nov. 9. Senate Democratic leader Chuck Schumer said the move shows Trump learned nothing from the midterm defeat.
top.why: Puts a hardline immigration architect in charge of the White House.

top.headline: Canada loses 4,700 jobs in October; unemployment rises to 6.7%
top.what: Statistics Canada says employment slipped slightly in October and the jobless rate rose 0.2 points to 6.7%, its highest since April.
top.why: Rising unemployment affects hiring and Bank of Canada decisions.

top.headline: Ottawa asks Competition Bureau to probe Stelco owner as layoffs loom
top.what: Industry Minister Mélanie Joly wants the competition commissioner to examine whether Cleveland-Cliffs breached the Competition Act at Stelco.
top.why: Hundreds of Hamilton steel jobs are at stake.

top.headline: Thousands of Ontario students walk out over OSAP cuts: 'We can't afford rent'
top.what: Thousands of students walked out over OSAP changes and tuition, while a separate freeze on student aid at career colleges drags on with no restart date.
top.why: Student aid cuts affect tuition and rent for Ontario students.
